name: hyper-elements
description: Write emails, web pages, PDFs and images as React components
readme:
Hyper Elements

Build emails, web pages, PDFs, and images with React.
One set of elements for developers and AI agents.

Quick start · AI agents · Test in email clients · Designs · Documentation · Website

Hyper Elements is an open-source React library for generating content. Write a receipt, invoice, landing page, or social card with typed elements. The engine handles layout and the markup each output needs, including email tables and responsive web HTML. - **Reuse your work across formats.** Share content, styles, and components between an email, its web version, and a PDF. - **Keep every output on brand.** Define colors, fonts, sizes, and element styles once in a theme, and every email, page, PDF, and image that uses it follows. - **Give agents useful feedback.** Validate designs, inspect layouts as text, and get diagnostics that explain where a problem is and how to fix it. - **Test existing HTML emails locally.** Check and preview Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail with the companion JavaScript library or CLI. Works with HTML from MJML, React Email or any email builder; no React required, no test sends, no account, nothing uploaded. - **Render in your own app.** Generate output on your server, with no browser, hosted service, or API key required.

## Quick start In a React project (React 18 or later): ```bash npm install @hyper-elements/react react react-dom ``` Build an order update, then render the same content as an email and a web page: ```tsx import { Button, Column, Email, Heading, Page, Text, render, } from "@hyper-elements/react"; function OrderUpdate({ name }: { name: string }) { return ( Thanks, {name}. Your order is on its way. ); } const content = ; const { html, text } = await render({content}); const { html: pageHtml } = await render({content}); ``` `html` and `text` are the email's HTML and plain text, ready for your [email provider](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/sending). `pageHtml` is a complete responsive web document. No client-side JavaScript is required. ## Choose your output Use the same layout and content elements under the root for your destination: | Build | Root | Render to | | --- | --- | --- | | Receipts, newsletters, transactional emails | `` | Email HTML and plain text with `render()` | | Landing pages, web versions of emails | `` | Responsive HTML with `render()` | | Invoices, reports, printable documents | `` | Print HTML with `render()`, or a PDF with [`renderPdf()`](./packages/react/docs/render-pdf.md) | | Social cards, Open Graph images, banners | `` | PNG or SVG with [`renderImage()`](./packages/react/docs/render-image.md) | The PDF and image renderers use separate imports and optional dependencies in Node.js. Diagnostics flag features a destination cannot represent. See [one invoice rendered as email, web, and PDF](./examples/content-workflows) for a complete example. ## Build with AI agents Give Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent the guide: ```bash npx skills add hyper-elements/hyper-elements ``` It offers three skills: [`hyper-elements`](./skills/hyper-elements/SKILL.md), the guide for writing designs; [`email-testing`](./skills/email-testing/SKILL.md), for previewing and checking any email (a design or HTML from anywhere) in Outlook, Gmail and the other clients; and [`brand-templates`](./skills/brand-templates/SKILL.md), for designs made from your team's templates, within their guardrails, and for writing templates. `--skill email-testing` installs that one alone. In Claude Code they're plugins too: `/plugin marketplace add hyper-elements/hyper-elements`, then `/plugin install email-testing@hyper-elements`, `/plugin install brand-templates@hyper-elements` or `/plugin install hyper-elements@hyper-elements`. Or add this to your project's `AGENTS.md` or agent rules: ```text Designs use Hyper Elements (@hyper-elements/react). If it isn't installed, install it with react and react-dom. Before writing a design, read node_modules/@hyper-elements/react/GUIDE.md. Validate the design, fix errors, review warnings, and inspect outline() before rendering. ``` The package includes `GUIDE.md` and `REFERENCE.md`, generated from its element definitions so they match the version you installed. Web-based agents can use [llms.txt](https://hyperelements.dev/llms.txt) or [llms-full.txt](https://hyperelements.dev/llms-full.txt). ### A feedback loop the agent can read `validate()` returns diagnostics with a code, severity, path in the design, and an actionable message. `outline()` shows the layout without making the agent read generated HTML. Try both on the quick-start component: ```tsx import { outline, validate } from "@hyper-elements/react"; const design = ; const report = validate(design); console.log(report.diagnostics); if (report.valid) console.log(outline(design)); ``` ```text Email 600px Column 600px Heading h1 536px "Thanks, Ada." Text 536px "Your order is on its way." Button: background #ef4638 "Track your order" → https://example.com/orders/10482 ``` An agent can spot missing content, incorrect widths, and layout mistakes before rendering, then see the email in each email client with the emulator below. The same loop runs from the shell, with no script, using [`@hyper-elements/cli`](./packages/cli) (`npm install -D @hyper-elements/cli`): `npx hyper-elements check emails/ --json` validates each design, `outline` prints its layout, `render` writes its HTML and plain text, and `preview` writes each email client's preview. Add `--findings` with the [browser setup below](#preview-and-test-emails-in-outlook-and-gmail-locally) to draw the previews and collect findings. Exit codes are stable (`1` when a design has errors) for agents and CI. [Agent setup and examples →](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/ai-agents) ## Preview and test emails in Outlook and Gmail locally `@hyper-elements/email-clients` is a free JavaScript and TypeScript library for checking existing HTML emails and previewing Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail locally. Give it the complete HTML from MJML, React Email, an email builder, or a hand-written email. No React is required, and the email is never sent or uploaded. An agent can do all of this from the [email-testing skill](./skills/email-testing/SKILL.md): the commands, each client's screenshot, and what it changed. ```bash npm install @hyper-elements/email-clients ``` Save this as `preview-email.mjs` beside your `email.html`: ```js import { mkdir, readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises"; import { renderInEmailClients } from "@hyper-elements/email-clients"; const html = await readFile("email.html", "utf8"); const { previews, diagnostics } = await renderInEmailClients(html, { emailClients: ["outlook", "gmail", "apple-mail"], }); await mkdir("out", { recursive: true }); for (const preview of previews) await writeFile(`out/${preview.filename}`, preview.html); console.log(diagnostics); ``` Run `node preview-email.mjs`, then open `out/outlook.html` in Chromium or Chrome. Each preview lists what the client changed. The same API takes a Hyper Elements design: `await renderInEmailClients()`. You can also check and preview an HTML email from the shell, with no script or React installation: ```bash npx @hyper-elements/cli check email.html npx @hyper-elements/cli preview email.html ``` The second command writes `out/clients/email/outlook.html` and the other client previews. To draw them and collect findings automatically, install the CLI and `playwright-core` together, and have Chrome, Edge or Playwright's Chromium installed: ```bash npm install -D @hyper-elements/cli playwright-core npx hyper-elements preview email.html --findings ``` If you need Chromium, download it once with `npx hyper-elements preview --install-browser`. See [browser setup and findings](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/cli#preview). Tested on Hyper Elements emails and on HTML emails built any other way, the emulator is 98% accurate on average against the real clients. Here's an example email template, a sign-in code, as the emulator draws it in four email clients:

[Email client emulator: supported clients, accuracy and options →](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/email-client-emulator) ## Agent Benchmarks ### Email In our benchmark of five email briefs, Hyper Elements reached a passing email **2.6× faster** with **3.4× fewer output tokens** than React Email, at the median. It was also **1.3× faster than MJML**. Hyper Elements and MJML both passed **16 of 16** first checks.

All four approaches ran in one interleaved batch, with 16 runs each against the same Chromium checks at desktop and mobile widths; all 64 eventually passed. Token counts here measure output tokens, not total usage or cost. [Methodology](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/benchmark) · [Reproduce the benchmark](./benchmark) ### Image Across five image briefs, Hyper Elements reached a passing image **1.65× faster** with **1.8× fewer output tokens** than Canvas 2D (`@napi-rs/canvas`), at the median. **17 of 20** images passed on the first check.

All 60 isolated runs passed the same text, font, image and layout checks: five briefs, four runs per brief per approach. The speed comparison with Playwright was inconclusive. [Methodology and results](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/benchmark#image-results) · [Reproduce the benchmark](./benchmark) ## Keep building - **Start from an example:** [Designs](https://hyperelements.dev/templates) · [Element gallery](https://hyperelements.dev/elements) - **Learn the API:** [Writing guide](./packages/react/GUIDE.md) · [Full reference](./packages/react/REFERENCE.md) - **Stay on brand:** [Themes](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/themes) - **Test in email clients:** [Email client emulator](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/email-client-emulator) · [Email client checks](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/diagnostics) - **Work from the shell:** [Command line](https://hyperelements.dev/docs/cli) · [`@hyper-elements/cli`](./packages/cli) - **Use it in your app:** [Next.js example](./examples/nextjs-app-router) · [Email providers](./packages/react/docs/email-providers.md) - **Bring existing templates:** [Migrate from React Email](./packages/react/docs/migrate-from-react-email.md) · [Move from Unlayer Elements](./packages/react/docs/migrating-from-unlayer-elements.md) - **Let teammates edit visually:** [Optional Unlayer editor integration](./packages/react/docs/visual-editing.md) ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Use the Node.js version in [`.nvmrc`](./.nvmrc) and pnpm 9.7 or later, then run `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow. ## License [MIT](./LICENSE). Built by the team behind [Unlayer](https://unlayer.com); works independently of the Unlayer platform.

<h1 align="center">Hyper Elements</h1>

<p align="center">

<strong>Build emails, web pages, PDFs, and images with React.</strong><br />

One set of elements for developers and AI agents.

</p>

<p align="center">

<a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@hyper-elements/react"><img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@hyper-elements/react.svg" alt="npm version" /></a>

<a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@hyper-elements/react"><img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@hyper-elements/react.svg" alt="Monthly downloads" /></a>

<a href="https://github.com/hyper-elements/hyper-elements/actions/workflows/test.yml"><img src="https://github.com/hyper-elements/hyper-elements/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg" alt="Tests" /></a>

</p>

<p align="center">

<a href="#quick-start">Quick start</a> ·

<a href="#build-with-ai-agents">AI agents</a> ·

<a href="#preview-and-test-emails-in-outlook-and-gmail-locally">Test in email clients</a> ·

<a href="https://hyperelements.dev/templates">Designs</a> ·

<a href="https://hyperelements.dev/docs">Documentation</a> ·

<a href="https://hyperelements.dev">Website</a>

</p>

Hyper Elements is an open-source React library for generating content. Write a receipt, invoice, landing page, or social card with typed elements. The engine handles layout and the markup each output needs, including email tables and responsive web HTML.

  • Reuse your work across formats. Share content, styles, and components between an email, its web version, and a PDF.
  • Keep every output on brand. Define colors, fonts, sizes, and element styles once in a theme, and every email, page, PDF, and image that uses it follows.
  • Give agents useful feedback. Validate designs, inspect layouts as text, and get diagnostics that explain where a problem is and how to fix it.
  • Test existing HTML emails locally. Check and preview Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail with the companion JavaScript library or CLI. Works with HTML from MJML, React Email or any email builder; no React required, no test sends, no account, nothing uploaded.
  • Render in your own app. Generate output on your server, with no browser, hosted service, or API key required.

<p align="center">

<img src="./apps/website/public/img/hyper-elements-overview.png" alt="React components flow through Hyper Elements into email HTML and plain text, responsive web HTML, PDF documents, and PNG or SVG images." width="1000" />

</p>

Quick start

In a React project (React 18 or later):


npm install @hyper-elements/react react react-dom

Build an order update, then render the same content as an email and a web page:


import {

  Button, Column, Email, Heading, Page, Text, render,

} from "@hyper-elements/react";



function OrderUpdate({ name }: { name: string }) {

  return (

    <Column style={{ padding: 32, gap: 16 }}>

      <Heading level={1}>Thanks, {name}.</Heading>

      <Text>Your order is on its way.</Text>

      <Button

        href="https://example.com/orders/10482"

        style={{ backgroundColor: "#ef4638", color: "#ffffff" }}

      >

        Track your order

      </Button>

    </Column>

  );

}



const content = <OrderUpdate name="Ada" />;

const { html, text } = await render(<Email width={600}>{content}</Email>);

const { html: pageHtml } = await render(<Page width={960}>{content}</Page>);

html and text are the email's HTML and plain text, ready for your email provider. pageHtml is a complete responsive web document. No client-side JavaScript is required.

Choose your output

Use the same layout and content elements under the root for your destination:

| Build | Root | Render to |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Receipts, newsletters, transactional emails | <Email> | Email HTML and plain text with render() |

| Landing pages, web versions of emails | <Page> | Responsive HTML with render() |

| Invoices, reports, printable documents | <Document> | Print HTML with render(), or a PDF with [renderPdf()](./packages/react/docs/render-pdf.md) |

| Social cards, Open Graph images, banners | <Canvas> | PNG or SVG with [renderImage()](./packages/react/docs/render-image.md) |

The PDF and image renderers use separate imports and optional dependencies in Node.js. Diagnostics flag features a destination cannot represent. See [one invoice rendered as email, web, and PDF](./examples/content-workflows) for a complete example.

Build with AI agents

Give Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent the guide:


npx skills add hyper-elements/hyper-elements

It offers three skills: [hyper-elements](./skills/hyper-elements/SKILL.md), the guide for writing designs;

[email-testing](./skills/email-testing/SKILL.md), for previewing and checking any email (a design or HTML from

anywhere) in Outlook, Gmail and the other clients; and [brand-templates](./skills/brand-templates/SKILL.md), for

designs made from your team's templates, within their guardrails, and for writing templates. --skill email-testing

installs that one alone.

In Claude Code they're plugins too: /plugin marketplace add hyper-elements/hyper-elements, then

/plugin install email-testing@hyper-elements, /plugin install brand-templates@hyper-elements or

/plugin install hyper-elements@hyper-elements.

Or add this to your project's AGENTS.md or agent rules:


Designs use Hyper Elements (@hyper-elements/react). If it isn't installed, install it

with react and react-dom. Before writing a design, read

node_modules/@hyper-elements/react/GUIDE.md.

Validate the design, fix errors, review warnings, and inspect outline() before rendering.

The package includes GUIDE.md and REFERENCE.md, generated from its element definitions so they match the version you installed. Web-based agents can use llms.txt or llms-full.txt.

A feedback loop the agent can read

validate() returns diagnostics with a code, severity, path in the design, and an actionable message. outline() shows the layout without making the agent read generated HTML. Try both on the quick-start component:


import { outline, validate } from "@hyper-elements/react";



const design = <Email width={600}><OrderUpdate name="Ada" /></Email>;

const report = validate(design);



console.log(report.diagnostics);

if (report.valid) console.log(outline(design));



Email 600px

  Column 600px

    Heading h1 536px "Thanks, Ada."

    Text 536px "Your order is on its way."

    Button: background #ef4638 "Track your order" → https://example.com/orders/10482

An agent can spot missing content, incorrect widths, and layout mistakes before rendering, then see the email in each email client with the emulator below.

The same loop runs from the shell, with no script, using [@hyper-elements/cli](./packages/cli) (npm install -D @hyper-elements/cli): npx hyper-elements check emails/ --json validates each design, outline prints its layout, render writes its HTML and plain text, and preview writes each email client's preview. Add --findings with the [browser setup below](#preview-and-test-emails-in-outlook-and-gmail-locally) to draw the previews and collect findings. Exit codes are stable (1 when a design has errors) for agents and CI.

Agent setup and examples →

<a id="test-it-in-email-clients"></a>

Preview and test emails in Outlook and Gmail locally

@hyper-elements/email-clients is a free JavaScript and TypeScript library for checking existing HTML emails and previewing Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail locally. Give it the complete HTML from MJML, React Email, an email builder, or a hand-written email. No React is required, and the email is never sent or uploaded.

An agent can do all of this from the [email-testing skill](./skills/email-testing/SKILL.md): the commands, each client's

screenshot, and what it changed.


npm install @hyper-elements/email-clients

Save this as preview-email.mjs beside your email.html:


import { mkdir, readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

import { renderInEmailClients } from "@hyper-elements/email-clients";



const html = await readFile("email.html", "utf8");

const { previews, diagnostics } = await renderInEmailClients(html, {

  emailClients: ["outlook", "gmail", "apple-mail"],

});

await mkdir("out", { recursive: true });

for (const preview of previews) await writeFile(`out/${preview.filename}`, preview.html);

console.log(diagnostics);

Run node preview-email.mjs, then open out/outlook.html in Chromium or Chrome. Each preview lists what the client changed. The same API takes a Hyper Elements design: await renderInEmailClients(<Email><OrderUpdate name="Ada" /></Email>).

You can also check and preview an HTML email from the shell, with no script or React installation:


npx @hyper-elements/cli check email.html

npx @hyper-elements/cli preview email.html

The second command writes out/clients/email/outlook.html and the other client previews. To draw them and collect findings automatically, install the CLI and playwright-core together, and have Chrome, Edge or Playwright's Chromium installed:


npm install -D @hyper-elements/cli playwright-core

npx hyper-elements preview email.html --findings

If you need Chromium, download it once with npx hyper-elements preview --install-browser. See browser setup and findings.

Tested on Hyper Elements emails and on HTML emails built any other way, the emulator is 98% accurate on average against the real clients. Here's an example email template, a sign-in code, as the emulator draws it in four email clients:

<p align="center">

<img src="./apps/website/public/generated/email-clients/keel-sign-in-code-outlook.png" alt="A sign-in code email in classic Outlook, drawn by the Hyper Elements email client emulator" width="230" />

<img src="./apps/website/public/generated/email-clients/keel-sign-in-code-gmail.png" alt="The sign-in code email in Gmail on the web, drawn by the emulator" width="230" />

<img src="./apps/website/public/generated/email-clients/keel-sign-in-code-apple-mail.png" alt="The sign-in code email in Apple Mail, drawn by the emulator" width="230" />

<img src="./apps/website/public/generated/email-clients/keel-sign-in-code-gmail-app.png" alt="The sign-in code email in the Gmail app on Android, drawn by the emulator" width="107" />

</p>

Email client emulator: supported clients, accuracy and options →

Agent Benchmarks

Email

In our benchmark of five email briefs, Hyper Elements reached a passing email 2.6× faster with 3.4× fewer output tokens than React Email, at the median. It was also 1.3× faster than MJML. Hyper Elements and MJML both passed 16 of 16 first checks.

<p align="center">

<a href="https://hyperelements.dev/docs/benchmark">

<img src="./apps/website/public/img/hyper-elements-agent-benchmark.svg" alt="Agent benchmark: Hyper Elements took 33 seconds, used 1,831 output tokens, and passed on the first check in 16 of 16 runs. MJML: 43 seconds, 2,762 output tokens, 16 of 16 first-check passes. Hand-written HTML: 60 seconds, 4,903 output tokens, 6 of 16 first-check passes. React Email: 86 seconds, 6,215 output tokens, 12 of 16 first-check passes. Time and token counts are medians." width="1000" />

</a>

</p>

All four approaches ran in one interleaved batch, with 16 runs each against the same Chromium checks at desktop and mobile widths; all 64 eventually passed. Token counts here measure output tokens, not total usage or cost. Methodology · [Reproduce the benchmark](./benchmark)

Image

Across five image briefs, Hyper Elements reached a passing image 1.65× faster with 1.8× fewer output tokens than Canvas 2D (@napi-rs/canvas), at the median. 17 of 20 images passed on the first check.

<p align="center">

<a href="https://hyperelements.dev/docs/benchmark#image-results">

<img src="./apps/website/public/img/hyper-elements-image-benchmark.svg" alt="Image agent benchmark: Hyper Elements took 76 seconds, used 5,096 output tokens, and passed on the first check in 17 of 20 runs. Playwright: 91 seconds, 6,846 output tokens, 14 of 20 first-check passes. Canvas 2D: 125 seconds, 9,132 output tokens, 16 of 20 first-check passes. Time and token counts are medians." width="1000" />

</a>

</p>

All 60 isolated runs passed the same text, font, image and layout checks: five briefs, four runs per brief per approach. The speed comparison with Playwright was inconclusive. Methodology and results · [Reproduce the benchmark](./benchmark)

Keep building

  • Start from an example: Designs · Element gallery
  • Learn the API: [Writing guide](./packages/react/GUIDE.md) · [Full reference](./packages/react/REFERENCE.md)
  • Stay on brand: Themes
  • Test in email clients: Email client emulator · Email client checks
  • Work from the shell: Command line · [@hyper-elements/cli](./packages/cli)
  • Use it in your app: [Next.js example](./examples/nextjs-app-router) · [Email providers](./packages/react/docs/email-providers.md)
  • Bring existing templates: [Migrate from React Email](./packages/react/docs/migrate-from-react-email.md) · [Move from Unlayer Elements](./packages/react/docs/migrating-from-unlayer-elements.md)
  • Let teammates edit visually: [Optional Unlayer editor integration](./packages/react/docs/visual-editing.md)

Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Use the Node.js version in [.nvmrc](./.nvmrc) and pnpm 9.7 or later, then run pnpm install, pnpm build, and pnpm test. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow.

License

[MIT](./LICENSE). Built by the team behind Unlayer; works independently of the Unlayer platform.
skillMd:
--- name: hyper-elements description: Write emails, web pages, printed documents, PDFs and images in code with Hyper Elements (@hyper-elements/react), React components that render email-safe HTML, responsive page HTML, print HTML, PDFs and PNG or SVG images. Use when writing or changing an Elements design, or when asked to build an email, page, document, PDF or image in code with Elements. --- # Hyper Elements Write emails, web pages, printed documents, PDFs and images in code with Hyper Elements (`npm install @hyper-elements/react`). This is the package's own guide to its elements at `@hyper-elements/react` (GUIDE.md in the package), written from their definitions: everything needed to write a design, in short. Every prop's and style's details, with its default: `node_modules/@hyper-elements/react/REFERENCE.md`. To test an email in Outlook, Gmail and other clients, a design or any HTML: the `email-testing` skill has the steps, or run `npx @hyper-elements/cli preview emails/welcome.tsx`. ## Before you write a design - If the project's package.json doesn't list `@hyper-elements/react`, install it: `npm install @hyper-elements/react react react-dom`, or the same with the project's package manager (`pnpm add`, `yarn add`, `bun add`). - Once it's installed, its own guide is `node_modules/@hyper-elements/react/GUIDE.md`, written for the version installed. `grep "hyper-elements guide" node_modules/@hyper-elements/react/GUIDE.md` gives its id; this skill's is `hyper-elements guide f82a37d3`. The same id: this skill is that guide, so read on. Another id, or none: read GUIDE.md and follow it where it differs from this skill. ## Templates from Unlayer Elements A project may have templates written with Unlayer Elements: they import `Body`, `ColumnLayouts` or `renderToHtml()` from `@unlayer/react-elements`, and use `values`, `layout`, `html` and style props such as `backgroundColor="#fff"`. Those components aren't in Hyper Elements, a new package: these are its components. - Move them with the codemod: `npx @hyper-elements/migrate src/emails --from unlayer-elements` lists what it would change, `--write` replaces the files (only those git can restore) and `--report notes.md` writes what it noted. It rewrites the imports and the JSX, and keeps props, loops and conditions. The new elements render with `await render(element)`, which is async, in place of `renderToHtml()`. More: `npx @hyper-elements/migrate --help`. - What the codemod can't move is listed, and the file is left as it was: rewrite that part by hand with these elements. - Then `npm install @hyper-elements/react`, and remove `@unlayer/react-elements` once nothing imports it. - Templates in React Email: `npx @hyper-elements/migrate src/emails` writes them in these elements and checks each against its original. ## How a design is written - Import from `@hyper-elements/react`. A design has one root: `Email`, `Page`, `Document` or `Canvas`. - Styles go in `style={{ … }}`, never as props: ``. A number is px; `padding` takes `16`, `[12, 24]` or `"12px 24px"`. A box's text styles are inherited by what it holds. - There are no margins: space between blocks is their parent's `gap` (``), space inside a box its `padding`. - A root, a `Section` and a `Column` stack their children. A `Row` puts its children side by side (each `Column` at its `style.width`, or an equal share) and stacks them on phones. `Grid columns={3}` makes rows of three. A `Section` is a band whose background spans the window; a `Column` with a background is a card. - Text is elements, not HTML: `Heading level={1}` and `Text` hold text; inside them `Span` styles a run, `Link href` links one, `LineBreak` breaks the line and `MergeTag name` writes a merge tag. No raw HTML (``, `
`, `
`) and no `html` prop. - `Image src={{ src, width, height }}` (the file's size in px) with `alt`; `style.width` sets the size shown. - An image's `src` is a public `https` URL the reader's email client can fetch: the project's own (its CDN, its other templates, its site) or one the person gives you. Never make one up: `example.com`, a guessed path or a file on this computer shows as a broken image. Where the design needs an image that doesn't exist yet, use a placeholder that loads, at the image's size: `https://placehold.co/1200x600/png?text=Product+screenshot` (width x height in px). Then tell the person which images to replace. A `data:` URI works in a Page, Document or Canvas, but Gmail doesn't show one in an Email. - Lists: `` of `ListItem`s. Tables: a `Table` of `TableRow`s (`header` on the first) of `TableCell`s, with `cellPadding` and `rowBorder` in the Table's `style`. - Phones: `style={{ fontSize: 24, mobile: { fontSize: 20 } }}` (the styles listed under "Phones", where `text` is fontSize, lineHeight, letterSpacing and textAlign), `hidden={{ mobile: true }}`; in an Email or a Page. Hover: `style={{ hover: { backgroundColor: "#374151" } }}` (those under "Hover"). - `await render(element)` gives `{ html, text, diagnostics }`; errors throw an `ElementsError` with the same `diagnostics`. `validate(element)` runs the checks without rendering; `outline(element)` prints the laid-out design (each block, its width, its text). - Templates (fixed parts, typed fields and checks): `@hyper-elements/react/template`. - Email clients: `@hyper-elements/email-clients`. `validate(email, { plugins: [await emailClients()] })` adds what classic Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail and others remove or change, naming its `clients`, with a `fix` (without it, one note: `email/more-checks`). To test an email in them, `await renderInEmailClients(email)` gives a preview per client: HTML that shows the email as that client does, in Chromium. It takes any other HTML email too. ```tsx import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises"; import { ElementsError, formatDiagnostics, render } from "@hyper-elements/react"; import Welcome from "./welcome"; try { const { html, diagnostics } = await render(); await writeFile("welcome.html", html); console.log(formatDiagnostics(diagnostics)); // warnings and notes, each with what to change } catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof ElementsError)) throw e; console.error(formatDiagnostics(e.diagnostics)); process.exitCode = 1; } ``` From the shell (`@hyper-elements/cli`): `npx hyper-elements check emails/welcome.tsx` runs these checks on the module's default export and exits 1 on errors (`--json` for JSON); `render` writes the HTML and text to `out/`. ## Common mistakes Each of these made an agent's first try fail: - `` → ``. Styles never go as props. - `` → ``, with the padding on a `Column` (a card) or a `Section` (a band) inside it. A root's width is a prop, and a root has no padding. - `items={[{ text: "Home", link: "/" }]}` → `items={[{ text: "Home", href: "/" }]}`. A `Menu`'s items are `{ text, href }`, a `Social`'s icons `{ name, href }`. - `style={{ marginBottom: 16 }}` → `gap: 16` on the parent. There are no margins. - `ColumnLayouts`, `layout`, `headingType`, `altText`, `html` are Unlayer Elements' props, not these: a `Row` of `Column`s, `level`, `alt`, and text as children. - `` → `src={{ src: "https://example.com/logo.png", width: 240, height: 80 }}`, the file's size. Without it, Outlook shows the file at its own size. - `mobile={{ fontSize: 20 }}`, `hover={{ … }}`, `_hover` or `md: { … }` → `style={{ fontSize: 24, mobile: { fontSize: 20 }, hover: { … } }}`. Phone and hover styles are blocks of `style`, and there's one breakpoint: phones. - `className="secondary"` or `sx={…}` → `variant="secondary"` (the theme's) or `style={{ apply: ["card"] }}`. ## Themes A theme is the brand, written once: `defineTheme({ colors, spacing, fontSizes, lineHeights, fonts, radii, elements, styles, formats })`, given to a root as `theme`. - In a design `token("colors.primary")` is a token's value, or part of one (`border: { width: 1, style: "solid", color: token("colors.border") }`); inside a theme, and only there, a token is `"{colors.primary}"`: everywhere in a design (a root's `style`, a scope's `tokens`) it is `token()`. Names are letters and digits: nest `gray.900`. - Roles: `colors.background` is the root's background; `colors.foreground`, `fonts.body`, `fontSizes.body` and `lineHeights.body` are its body text (color, font, size and line height), which Text, table cells and list items inherit: set body text here, not on `Text` (a style on `Text` misses table cells). `fonts.heading` is a Heading's font, `colors.primary` and `colors.primaryForeground` a Button's (`colors.primary` a Link's) and `fontSizes.body` its size too, `colors.border` a Divider's. - `elements.Button: { … }` is every Button's default style; `by: { level: { 1: { fontSize: 40 } } }` sets one by a prop's value (a type scale); `variants: { secondary: { … } }` are picked with `variant="secondary"` (a list merges in order). - `styles: { card: { … } }` are named styles: `style={{ apply: ["card"], padding: 8 }}`. A key an element sets itself also replaces the theme's phone and hover values for it. - `tokens` on a Section, Row, Column or Grid overrides tokens inside it: an inverted band is `
`. - `formats: { email: { … } }` overrides it for one kind of root; `extendTheme(base, overrides)` makes a brand's or a customer's theme from a shared one; `declare module "@hyper-elements/react" { interface Register { theme: typeof brand } }` types every name. ## A whole design ```tsx import { Button, Column, defineTheme, Email, Heading, Image, Link, List, ListItem, MergeTag, Text, Row, Span, Table, TableCell, TableRow, token } from "@hyper-elements/react"; // The brand, once: every Email, Page, Document and Canvas that takes it is on brand. const acme = defineTheme({ colors: { background: "#f4f4f5", foreground: "#18181b", primary: "#111827", primaryForeground: "#ffffff", muted: "#71717a", border: "#e4e4e7" }, fonts: { body: "Inter, Arial, sans-serif" }, elements: { Heading: { by: { level: { 1: { fontSize: 24, mobile: { fontSize: 20 } } } } }, Button: { borderRadius: 6, hover: { backgroundColor: "#374151" } }, }, styles: { card: { backgroundColor: "#ffffff", padding: 32, gap: 16, borderRadius: 8 } }, }); export default function Receipt() { return ( Thanks for your order, Order #10482 ships tomorrow. Track it. Item Price Linen shirt $48.00
Shipping to Ada Lovelace, London Next steps We pack it You track it Acme Inc., 1 Market St, San Francisco ); } ``` ## A Canvas as an image `renderImage(element, options)` (`@hyper-elements/react/image`) writes a `Canvas` as a PNG (`format: "svg"` an SVG, `scale: 2` twice the pixels). Nothing is fetched: `fonts` gives each font file by the family the design names (TTF, OTF or WOFF, not WOFF2; one per weight and style used), `images` each image file by the `src` the design gives. It gives `{ image, width, height, diagnostics }` (what it drew otherwise: a weight not given, a hover); errors throw an `ElementsError`. ```tsx import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises"; import { Canvas, Heading, Image } from "@hyper-elements/react"; import { renderImage } from "@hyper-elements/react/image"; const { image, diagnostics } = await renderImage( Launch week , { fonts: [{ family: "Inter", src: await readFile("Inter-Bold.ttf"), weight: 700 }], images: { "https://example.com/logo.png": await readFile("logo.png") }, } ); ``` ## Elements \* required. *text* styles: color, fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, fontStyle, lineHeight, letterSpacing, textAlign, textTransform. *box* styles: width, maxWidth, padding, backgroundColor, border, borderRadius. ### Roots - **Email**: An email. Its children are stacked down the content width, centered in the window. Holds sections, layout, blocks. Props: width (a length (a number of px)), previewText (text), title (text), lang (text), dir (ltr|rtl|auto), fonts (fontFaces). Style: text, backgroundColor, gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch). Phones: text, gap. - **Page**: A web page. Its children are stacked down the content width, centered in the window. Holds sections, layout, blocks. Props: width (a length (a number of px)), description (text), breakpoints (breakpoints), title (text), lang (text), dir (ltr|rtl|auto), fonts (fontFaces). Style: text, backgroundColor, gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch). Phones: gap. - **Document**: A printed document: its children on pages of its size (Document.Page, or split by PageBreaks), a PageHeader and a PageFooter on each. Renders to print HTML, and to PDF with @hyper-elements/react/pdf. Holds sections, layout, blocks, Document.Page, PageBreak, PageHeader, PageFooter. Props: size (A3|A4|A5|Letter|Legal|Tabloid), orientation (portrait|landscape), margin (insets), title (text), lang (text), dir (ltr|rtl|auto), fonts (fontFaces). Style: text, backgroundColor, gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch). - **Canvas**: An image of a fixed size (a social card, a banner): its children laid out in it as on a page. Written as PNG or SVG with @hyper-elements/react/image. Holds sections, layout, blocks. Props: width (a length (a number of px)), height (a length (a number of px)), title (text), lang (text), dir (ltr|rtl|auto), fonts (fontFaces). Style: text, backgroundColor, gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch), padding, justifyContent (start|center|end|space-between). ### Sections and layout - **Section**: A band across the whole window, directly in an Email or Page: its background spans the window, its children are stacked at the content width. Holds layout, blocks. Style: text, backgroundColor, padding, border, gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch). Phones: text, padding, border, gap. - **Row**: Lays its children out side by side. A child takes its width, or a share of what's left (its flex, 1 by default). Holds layout, blocks. Props: stackOnMobile (true or false), dir (ltr|rtl|auto). Style: text, box, minWidth, height, overflow (visible|hidden), gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch), justifyContent (start|center|end|space-between), flexWrap (nowrap|wrap|words), flex. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, padding, border, gap. - **Column**: Stacks its children vertically, with its own spacing and box. Holds layout, blocks. Style: text, box, minWidth, height, overflow (visible|hidden), gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch), justifyContent (start|center|end|space-between), flex. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, padding, border, gap. - **Grid**: Its children in columns of equal width, row after row; on phones, one under another. Holds layout, blocks. Props: columns (an integer from 1 to 12), stackOnMobile (true or false). Style: text, box, minWidth, height, overflow (visible|hidden), gap, rowGap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch), flex. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, padding, border, gap, rowGap. - **Layer**: Its children over each other, in one box as tall as the tallest: words on an image (a background image, its first child). In an email, an Image with one child over it. Holds layout, blocks. Style: text, width, minWidth, maxWidth, backgroundColor, border, borderRadius, height, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch), justifyItems (start|center|end|stretch), flex. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, border. ### Blocks - **Svg**: Shapes (Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Line, Polygon, Path) drawn in a box of its own: its width and height, and the coordinates its viewBox gives them. Not in an Email. Holds shapes. Props: width* (a number from 0), height* (a number from 0), viewBox (text), title (text). Style: padding, backgroundColor, border, borderRadius, flex. Phones: padding, border. - **Text**: A paragraph of text. Holds text, inline, Image. Props: dir (ltr|rtl|auto), fit ({ sizes, maxLines }). Style: text, box, textDecoration (none|underline|line-through), flex. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, padding, border. - **Heading**: A heading, from level 1 (the page's title) to 6. Holds text, inline. Props: level (1|2|3|4|5|6), dir (ltr|rtl|auto), fit ({ sizes, maxLines }). Style: text, box, textDecoration (none|underline|line-through), flex. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, padding, border. - **Button**: A link drawn as a button. Holds text, Span, MergeTag, LineBreak. Props: href* (link), title (text), aria-label (text), attrs (attributes). Style: text, box, textDecoration (none|underline|line-through), boxSizing (border-box|content-box), alignSelf (start|center|end), flex. Hover: color, backgroundColor. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, padding, border, alignSelf. - **Image**: An image in the content. Without a width it takes its own size, no wider than its parent. Props: src* (asset), alt (text), title (text). Style: width, maxWidth, height, border, borderRadius, flex, alignSelf (start|center|end), verticalAlign (top|middle). Phones: width, maxWidth, border, alignSelf. - **Divider**: A horizontal line. Style: borderTop, width, padding. Phones: width, padding. - **List**: A bulleted or numbered list of ListItems. Its markers sit in a column of their own (indent) before the items. Holds ListItem. Props: type (bullet|number), start (an integer from 0). Style: text, width, maxWidth, padding, backgroundColor, border, gap, indent, flex. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, padding, border, gap. - **Table**: A table of data: TableRows of TableCells. Columns take their cells' widths; the rest share what's left. Holds TableRow. Style: text, width, maxWidth, backgroundColor, border, cellPadding, rowBorder, borderCollapse (separate|collapse), flex. Phones: text, width, maxWidth, border. - **Video**: A YouTube or Vimeo video: its player on a page; in an email (which can't play one), its thumbnail, linked to it. Props: src* (video), thumbnail (asset), title (text). Style: width, maxWidth, flex. Phones: width, maxWidth. - **Social**: Links to social profiles: a line of the networks' icons, each linked to its profile. Props: icons* (a list of icons, each { name, href }), iconType (circle|rounded|squared), size (an integer from 1). Style: gap, justifyContent (start|center|end), flex. Phones: gap. - **Menu**: A line of links (a site's sections, a footer's), onto more lines where they don't fit, with a separator between them on desktop; or links down a column. Props: items* (a list of items, each { text, href }), separator (text), layout (horizontal|vertical). Style: color, fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, lineHeight, letterSpacing, textTransform (none|uppercase|lowercase|capitalize), separatorColor, padding, justifyContent (start|center|end), flex. Phones: fontSize, lineHeight, letterSpacing. - **Html**: Markup written as it is, for what no element says (the builder's HTML block): in an email and on a page as given, nothing in it checked or escaped. A Document's PDF and a Canvas's image draw its plain text. Props: html* (text), text (text). ### Inline - **PageNumber**: In a Document's text: the number of the page it's on, or (total) how many pages there are. Only in a Document. Props: total (true or false). - **Span**: Styled text inside text; raised or lowered (superscript, subscript) with verticalAlign. Holds text, inline. Style: color, fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, fontStyle (normal|italic), letterSpacing, textTransform (none|uppercase|lowercase|capitalize), textDecoration (none|underline|line-through), backgroundColor, verticalAlign (baseline|super|sub). Phones: fontSize, letterSpacing. - **Link**: A link: text inside text, or around an Image. Holds text, inline, Image. Props: href* (link), title (text), aria-label (text), attrs (attributes). Style: color, fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, fontStyle (normal|italic), letterSpacing, textTransform (none|uppercase|lowercase|capitalize), textDecoration (none|underline|line-through), backgroundColor, flex. Hover: color, textDecoration, backgroundColor. Phones: fontSize, letterSpacing. - **LineBreak**: Starts a new line inside text. - **MergeTag**: A value the sending service fills in (a name, a link), written in the service's own syntax. Props: name* (text). ### Parts - **Document.Page**: One page of a Document (Document.Page in JSX): its children stacked down it, inside the Document's margins. Holds sections, layout, blocks. Style: text, backgroundColor, gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch). - **PageBreak**: In a Document, where a page ends: what follows starts the next page. - **PageHeader**: In a Document: drawn at the top of every page, inside its margins. Holds layout, blocks. Style: text, padding, backgroundColor, border, gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch). - **PageFooter**: In a Document: drawn at the bottom of every page, inside its margins. Holds layout, blocks. Style: text, padding, backgroundColor, border, gap, alignItems (start|center|end|stretch). - **ListItem**: An item of a List: text, and a List of its own to nest one. Holds text, inline, List. Props: dir (ltr|rtl|auto). Style: text, textDecoration (none|underline|line-through). Phones: text. - **TableRow**: A row of a Table. A header row's cells are header cells, in bold. Holds TableCell. Props: header (true or false), footer (true or false). Style: text, backgroundColor, height. Phones: text. - **TableCell**: A cell of a TableRow: text, and images. Its width sets its column's. Holds text, inline, Image. Props: colSpan (an integer from 1), dir (ltr|rtl|auto). Style: text, textDecoration (none|underline|line-through), padding, backgroundColor, border, width, verticalAlign (top|middle|bottom). Phones: text, padding, border. ### Shapes - **Rect**: A rectangle at x, y in its Svg, rounded by rx. Props: x (a number), y (a number), width* (a number from 0), height* (a number from 0), rx (a number from 0). Style: fill, stroke, strokeWidth, opacity. - **Circle**: A circle centered at cx, cy in its Svg. Props: cx (a number), cy (a number), r* (a number from 0). Style: fill, stroke, strokeWidth, opacity. - **Ellipse**: An ellipse centered at cx, cy in its Svg. Props: cx (a number), cy (a number), rx* (a number from 0), ry* (a number from 0). Style: fill, stroke, strokeWidth, opacity. - **Line**: A straight line from x1, y1 to x2, y2 in its Svg (drawn by its stroke). Props: x1 (a number), y1 (a number), x2 (a number), y2 (a number). Style: fill, stroke, strokeWidth, opacity. - **Polygon**: A closed shape through its points ("0,0 40,0 20,30"), in its Svg. Props: points* (text). Style: fill, stroke, strokeWidth, opacity. - **Path**: A shape drawn by an SVG path (d), in its Svg. Props: d* (text). Style: fill, stroke, strokeWidth, opacity. ## Values - *fontFaces*: a list of { family, src, format, weight, style } - *color*: a color ("#0879a1", "rgb(…)", "rgba(…)" or a CSS name) - *fontFamily*: a font stack, as CSS writes it ("Inter, Arial, sans-serif") - *fontWeight*: 100 to 900 in hundreds, "normal" or "bold" - *lineHeight*: a multiple of the font size (1.5), a percentage ("150%"), px ("24px") or "normal" (the font's own) - *breakpoints*: { mobile }: the phone width in px (from 240) - *insets*: px for all sides, "8px 16px" (1 to 4 values), [v, h] or [t, r, b, l], or { top, right, bottom, left } - *border*: "1px solid #ccc", { width, style, color } for all sides, or { top, right, bottom, left } with one of those each - *radius*: px for every corner, [topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft], or { topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft } - *flex*: a share of the free width (0 or more), or "none" - *link*: a URL (http, https, mailto, tel, a path, or a merge tag) or { href, target } - *attributes*: attributes by name, each a text value (no on… handlers, href or style) - *asset*: an image URL (http, https or a data:image URI), or { src, width, height } - *line*: "1px solid #ccc" or { width, style, color } - *video*: a YouTube or Vimeo video's https link
